## https://8pck.com/answers/bottle-tooling-cost/
Title: How much does a new bottle mould cost? | 8PCK
Description: A new blow mould is about USD 800 and takes 15–20 days. An injection mould for a cap is USD 1,500–3,000, because the tool is more complex.
Sections: The Number, and What It Covers; When the Mould Is Not Needed; Part Count Before Size; Why Two Quotes Differ; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: How much does a new bottle mould cost? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / How much does a new bottle mould cost? How Much Does a New Bottle Mould Cost? A new blow mould is about USD 800 and takes 15–20 days. An injection mould for a cap is USD 1,500–3,000, because the tool is more complex. The Number, and What It Covers A blow mould for a bottle body is quoted around USD 850 and 15–20 days. That covers the tool, a trial run and the first samples. An injection mould for a closure costs more — USD 1,500–3,000 — because a cap has more geometry. When the Mould Is Not Needed With 3,000+ moulds in stock, most briefs can be matched to an existing shape. Then there is no tooling cost and the minimum stays at 1,000 pcs per colour. Part Count Before Size One cavity on a simple blow mould starts around USD 850. An injection mould for a cap starts near 3,700. A four-part assembly lands at 16,000–27,500, because each part is its own tool and trial. A thread that must be unscrewed adds 30–45 % to that part; a mirror polish adds days rather than dollars. Why Two Quotes Differ Steel grade, heat treatment, polish and the number of trial shots included. A cheap tool runs fine for 30,000 shots and starts flashing at 80,000 — rational for a one-season launch, false economy for a repeat line. Ask two questions of any tooling quote: which steel, and how many shots it is expected to run. Frequently Asked Is the mould mine? Yes — the tool belongs to the customer who paid for it. Can I get the mould moved? Yes, after the invoices for the tool are settled. How long does a new shape take in total? 15–20 days for the tool, then 7 days for samples and 25–35 days for production. Is tooling refundable? No. It is a one-off, and it belongs to the customer. Can the tool move to another factory? Yes, on instruction — it is the customer's property. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. Title: What documents do I need to import plastic bottles into the EU?
Description: For plastic food-contact bottles: the resin declaration of compliance, a migration test report against EU 10/2011, and a statement of compliance for the fi
Sections: The Three Documents; What the Migration Test Actually Measures; What Is Often Missing; Where the Importer Sits; The Two Documents That Matter; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: What documents do I need to import plastic bottles into the EU? Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / What documents do I need to import plastic bottles into the EU? What Documents Do I Need to Import Plastic Bottles into the EU? For plastic food-contact bottles: the resin declaration of compliance, a migration test report against EU 10/2011, and a statement of compliance for the finished article. Add RoHS if the pack has printing or electronic components. The Three Documents A declaration of compliance (DoC) from the resin supplier, a migration test report on the finished article against EU 10/2011, and a statement of compliance issued for the pack you are importing. The DoC covers the material; the migration test covers the finished article; the statement ties them to your order. What the Migration Test Actually Measures Overall migration (the total mass that can transfer to food) and, where relevant, specific migration of monomers. It is run with food simulants — aqueous, acidic, fatty — matched to what the pack will hold. What Is Often Missing The declaration covers the resin lot, not the finished bottle, and it is rarely per shipment. Ask for the declaration with the order, and keep the lot number on file. For recycled content, add the grade and percentage — mass balance is not the same as physical recycled content. Where the Importer Sits The importer is the responsible operator in the EU. The supplier provides the documentation; the importer holds it and can be asked for it by the authorities. That is why the documents are worth collecting before the container ships, not after. The Two Documents That Matter The EU 10/2011 declaration of conformity for the material, and the migration test report that supports it. Both are per grade, not per customer, and both should carry a laboratory name and a date. For cosmetics, the packaging also needs a statement on heavy metals and, where relevant, recycled content. Frequently Asked What is EU 10/2011? The EU regulation on plastic food-contact materials; it sets the migration limits the test report checks. Do I need a migration test for every order? Not for every order, but for the material and process combination; the declaration should cover the lot. Is RoHS needed for bottles? For printed or electronic packs, yes; for a plain bottle it is usually the printing inks that matter. Who is responsible in the EU? The importer is the responsible operator and must hold the documentation. Do I need the originals? A scanned signed copy is accepted by most importers; the original travels with the goods on request. Who issues it? The factory, on its letterhead, backed by the laboratory report. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. ## https://8pck.com/answers/how-to-choose-closure/
Title: How do I choose the right closure? | 8PCK
Description: Start from the product: water-thin takes a flip-top or sprayer, lotion takes a pump, oil takes a dropper. The neck follows the closure, not the other way r
Sections: The Order of Decisions; The Compatibility Trap; The Closure Follows the Neck; Dose and Feel; What Breaks First; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: How do I choose the right closure? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / How do I choose the right closure? How Do I Choose the Right Closure? Start from the product: water-thin takes a flip-top or sprayer, lotion takes a pump, oil takes a dropper. The neck follows the closure, not the other way round. The Order of Decisions Viscosity first, then dose, then one-handed use, then the look. Doing it in the other order is how a 24/410 pump ends up on a 50 ml bottle that looks top-heavy. The Compatibility Trap 410 and 415 thread the same diameter but not the same height: a 410 cap threads onto a 415 neck and weeps. Confirm the thread code on the drawing, not the photo. The Closure Follows the Neck 24/410 takes a lotion pump, a disc-top or a flip-top; 28/410 takes a heavier pump; 20/410 takes a fine mist sprayer or a small pump; 18/410 is the dropper neck. The mistake is choosing the closure first and discovering the neck afterwards — that is where 'the pump does not fit' comes from. Dose and Feel A pump is a dose device: 1.2 ml per stroke for a lotion, 2 ml for a body wash. The bottle has to deliver that dose to the last third of the fill, which is why the dip tube length and the base shape matter as much as the pump. A disc-top is cheap and gives no dose control; a fine mist sprayer needs a low-viscosity liquid, not a gel. What Breaks First On a lotion pump it is the spring, when a high-salt formula corrodes it. On a sprayer it is the nozzle, when a viscous product clogs it. On a disc-top it is the hinge, after a few thousand openings. All three are testable in a week with the real formula, and none are fixable after the container ships. Frequently Asked What is the most common neck? 24/410 covers most 250–500 ml cosmetics. Can I change the closure later? Yes, if the neck stays the same. Do you test the pair? Yes — the closure is fitted and leak-tested on the filled bottle. Can I use a pump on a 28/410 bottle? Yes, a 28/410 pump — not a 24/410 one. Does the closure change the MOQ? Yes: 1,000 pcs per closure type. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. ## https://8pck.com/answers/incoterms-explained/
Title: EXW, FOB or CIF — which should I choose? | 8PCK
Description: FOB Shantou is the usual choice for a first order: the factory handles export clearance and you control the freight.
Sections: What Each One Means in Practice; Why FOB Usually Wins; What Each Term Puts on You; Where the Risk Actually Moves; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: EXW, FOB or CIF — which should I choose? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / EXW, FOB or CIF — which should I choose? EXW, FOB or CIF — Which Should I Choose? FOB Shantou is the usual choice for a first order: the factory handles export clearance and you control the freight. What Each One Means in Practice EXW: you arrange collection, export clearance and freight. lowest unit cost on paper, most work in reality. FOB: the factory delivers to the port and clears export; you book the ocean. CIF: the factory also pays freight to your port, which is simple but removes your control over the forwarder. Why FOB Usually Wins FOB keeps the freight visible and lets you use your own forwarder, which matters when something goes wrong in transit. What Each Term Puts on You EXW: you collect from Shantou, and you carry export clearance. FOB: the factory delivers to the port and clears export; you pay freight and insurance. CIF: the factory arranges freight and insurance to your port, but the risk still passes at the ship's rail. For a first order, FOB is the clearest: the cost split is visible and the forwarder is yours. Where the Risk Actually Moves Under FOB, risk passes when the goods are on board, not when they reach your warehouse. Insurance is yours from that point, and it costs less than most buyers expect. Under CIF the factory arranges insurance, but the cover is minimum — 110 % of the invoice, institute clauses C. If the pack is fragile, buy your own. Frequently Asked Which is lowest unit cost? EXW on paper, but the hidden cost is export clearance. Can you quote CIF? Yes, to your nearest port. Who handles insurance? On FOB, you do; on CIF, we do, at minimum cover. Which is cheapest? EXW looks cheapest and usually is not, once export clearance and inland haulage are added. Can you quote DDP? Yes, through a forwarder, as an indicative landed cost. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. ## https://8pck.com/answers/minimum-order-quantity/
Title: What is the MOQ for custom plastic bottles? | 8PCK
Description: 1,000 pcs per colour on an existing mould. A new bottle mould costs about USD 800 and takes 15–20 days; spray coating and metallising start at 3,000 pcs; s
Sections: How the Number Is Calculated; The Number by Product Type; What Happens Below the MOQ; Tooling, if the Shape Is New; Why the MOQ Is per Colour; Where the 1,000 Comes From; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: What is the MOQ for custom plastic bottles? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / What is the MOQ for custom plastic bottles? What Is the MOQ for Custom Plastic Bottles? 1,000 pcs per colour on an existing mould. A new bottle mould costs about USD 800 and takes 15–20 days; spray coating and metallising start at 3,000 pcs; soft tubes at 3,000; printed pouches at 10,000. How the Number Is Calculated Changeover Time Purging the machine and checking the shade takes the same time at 500 pcs as at 5,000, so below 1,000 it dominates the unit price. Decoration Floors Silkscreen plates are a one-off at 1,000; spray coat and metallising need 3,000 because the line set-up is heavier. Material Minimums Resin is bought in 25 kg bags and colour masterbatch in batches; the MOQ is set where a clean run is possible. The Number by Product Type Bottles, jars and airless packs: 1,000 pcs per colour, per size. Spray coat, hot stamp and metallising: 3,000 pcs because the set-up is the cost. Soft tubes: 3,000 pcs per design. Printed stand-up pouches: 10,000 pcs, because each colour needs a rotogravure cylinder. Closures ordered on their own follow the same rule: 1,000 pcs per type, and mixed closures within one neck size can share a carton. What Happens Below the MOQ Two options. Order a stock colour of a stock mould and print your label, which can run from a few hundred pieces with a digital label. Or accept that a custom colour needs a minimum batch: the machine has to run a full changeover either way, so the price per piece rises steeply under 1,000. Alternatively we have sold 500 pcs on a stock mould when the customer accepts a stock colour. It is an exception, not a rule, and it is quoted per case. Tooling, if the Shape Is New With 3,000+ moulds on the shelf, most briefs match an existing shape. When they do not, a new blow mould is about USD 850 and 15–20 days, and it belongs to the customer — we do not re-use a customer's mould for anyone else. Injection moulds for a new closure are a separate cost and are quoted after the closure design is fixed. Why the MOQ Is per Colour A colour change means purging the machine, checking the shade against a standard, and scrapping the transition material. That run is the same whether you order 1,000 or 20,000, so the 1,000 minimum is the point where the changeover stops dominating the unit price. Where the 1,000 Comes From It is the point at which a stock mould run is worth loading. Below that the set-up time per piece climbs and the factory loses money — which is why a 500-piece request is usually answered with a stock colour rather than a colour match. Decoration has its own floor: silkscreen at 1,000, spray coat and metallising at 3,000. A mixed order carries the minimum for each colour, not for the order. Frequently Asked What is the minimum order for custom plastic bottles? 1,000 pcs per colour on an existing mould; 3,000 for spray coat or a soft tube; 10,000 for a printed pouch. How much does a new bottle mould cost? About USD 800 for a blow mould, with 15–20 days for tooling. The mould belongs to the customer. Can I order 500 pieces? Only on a stock mould in a stock colour, quoted case by case. A custom colour starts at 1,000. Can I mix colours in one order? Yes, but each colour carries the 1,000-piece minimum. What if I only need 300? Stock colours from inventory, or a stock shape with a label rather than a print. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. Title: What are the payment terms? | 8PCK
Description: 30 % deposit on order, 70 % against the bill of lading. Payment goes to CXWN, the factory — 8PCK does not invoice.
Sections: The Standard Split; Who Invoices; Why 30/70; What the Paperwork Protects; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: What are the payment terms? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / What are the payment terms? What Are the Payment Terms? 30 % deposit on order, 70 % against the bill of lading. Payment goes to CXWN, the factory — 8PCK does not invoice. The Standard Split Thirty percent deposit to start production, seventy percent against the copy of the bill of lading. That is the standard arrangement for a first order and it protects both sides: the factory is not financing the resin, and the buyer is not paying in full before the goods ship. Who Invoices CXWN issues the contract and the invoice. 8PCK is the export desk: we handle the English, the specification and the follow-up, but the commercial documents are the factory's. Why 30/70 The deposit covers resin and machine time; the balance is released against the bill of lading copy, when the goods exist and are on board. Neither side is exposed for the whole order. For repeat customers the split sometimes moves to 20/80; for a first order with a new mould it does not. What the Paperwork Protects The contract names the specification, the quantity and the tolerance. The invoice matches it. If a batch fails inspection, the payment terms are what makes a remedy possible — which is why the balance is against documents, not against arrival. Frequently Asked Can I pay by letter of credit? Yes, for larger orders; the bank charges are shared as agreed in the contract. Is the deposit refundable? It covers resin and tool time, so it is not refundable once production starts. Who do I pay? CXWN, the factory. The invoice comes from them. Can I pay on delivery? Not on a first order. After two clean orders, terms are negotiable. Which currency? USD, by bank transfer to CXWN. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. Title: How much does a custom plastic bottle cost? | 8PCK
Description: At 10,000 pcs, a 500 ml PET bottle at 28 g with a lotion pump typically lands around USD 0.15–0.35 per unit FOB Shantou. The pump can be 40–60 % of that; r
Sections: Where the Money Goes; The Four Things That Set the Price; Why the Pump Matters More Than the Bottle; What Changes the Price at the MOQ Boundary; How to Get a Number You Can Compare; What Actually Moves the Price; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: How much does a custom plastic bottle cost? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / How much does a custom plastic bottle cost? How Much Does a Custom Plastic Bottle Cost? At 10,000 pcs, a 500 ml PET bottle at 28 g with a lotion pump typically lands around USD 0.15–0.35 per unit FOB Shantou. The pump can be 40–60 % of that; resin is roughly half of the bottle's own cost. Where the Money Goes Resin 40–55 % of the bottle cost. A 500 ml PET at 28 g and at 36 g differ by roughly 25 % in material. Closure A standard lotion pump is a few cents; a foam or fine-mist pump can be several times that, and on a 30 ml serum it is the most expensive part. Decoration and Packing 5–25 % depending on method; packing density also changes freight, which is often the largest line on the invoice. The Four Things That Set the Price Bottle weight in grams, colour, decoration and packing density. Resin is bought by the tonne, so a 28 g bottle and a 40 g bottle differ by about 40 % in material before anyone touches a machine. Colour: stock (no charge), masterbatch (one changeover), or spray coat (3,000 pcs minimum and a separate process). Decoration: silkscreen from 1,000 pcs, labels lower in unit cost for multi-colour art, hot stamp and metallising from 3,000. Why the Pump Matters More Than the Bottle A standard lotion pump is a few cents; a foam pump or a fine mist sprayer can be several times that. On a 30 ml serum the closure is often the most expensive component in the pack, and on a 500 ml shampoo the pump is 40–60 % of the unit price. This is why two quotes for 'the same' 500 ml bottle can differ by 30 %: one has a standard pump, the other a foam pump with a custom collar. What Changes the Price at the MOQ Boundary Under 1,000 pcs, the changeover dominates and the price per unit rises sharply. Between 1,000 and 10,000 the price falls mostly from packing density and freight, not from the moulding itself. Above 20,000, resin price and payment terms matter more than labour. How to Get a Number You Can Compare Send four things: capacity, neck finish, material and quantity, plus the closure you have in mind. We quote unit price, packing data (pcs per carton, carton size, gross weight) and lead time together, so the freight calculation is yours to check rather than a guess. Prices above are indicative for 2026 resin levels and FOB Shantou; every quote is issued per order by the factory. What Actually Moves the Price Resin weight first, then decoration, then quantity. A 500 ml PET at 28 g and the same at 22 g differ by roughly 20 % on material alone; four-colour silkscreen can add more than the bottle. Freight is the line buyers forget: a heavier bottle costs more per container as well as per piece. Frequently Asked How much is a 500 ml plastic bottle? Indicatively USD 0.15–0.35 per unit FOB at 10,000 pcs including a standard lotion pump, depending on weight, colour and decoration. Why is there no price list? Resin prices move weekly and the closure can double the unit cost, so a fixed list would be wrong within a month. We quote per order within 24 hours. What is the lowest unit cost way to lower the unit price? Reduce bottle weight, use a stock colour, use a label instead of a spray coat, and order in the largest packing multiple you can store. Why is my price different from last year? Resin and freight move quarterly. A quote is usually held for 30 days. Is a bigger order always cheaper per piece? Cheaper per piece, not always cheaper in total — and the saving flattens after about 30,000. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. ## https://8pck.com/answers/production-lead-time/
Title: What is the lead time for custom plastic bottles from China? | 8PCK
Description: Samples in 7 days from a stock mould; production 25–35 days after sample approval; add 15–20 days if new tooling is needed. Sea freight adds about 30–35 da
Sections: What Runs in Parallel; The Timeline, Step by Step; What Actually Delays an Order; Shipping After Production; How to Plan a Launch Date; The Three Queues; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: What is the lead time for custom plastic bottles from China? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / What is the lead time for custom plastic bottles from China? What Is the Lead Time for Custom Plastic Bottles From China? Samples in 7 days from a stock mould; production 25–35 days after sample approval; add 15–20 days if new tooling is needed. Sea freight adds about 30–35 days to the US and 30–40 to Europe. What Runs in Parallel Artwork Artwork approval is the usual delay, and it sits with the customer. Send it at sample stage so it runs in parallel. Colour Matching A physical colour standard takes 3–5 days; matching to a Pantone number is faster and less exact. Inspection and Booking Third-party inspection and container booking add 3–7 days after production that most timelines forget. The Timeline, Step by Step Day 0: brief with capacity, neck, material, quantity and market. Day 1–2: specification and quotation. Day 3–7: sample from the production mould, not a showroom piece. Day 7–10: sample approval and deposit. Day 10–45: production, 25–35 days depending on the line. Day 45+: inspection, packing, shipment. If the shape is new, insert 15–20 days for tooling before sampling. What Actually Delays an Order Three things, in order: artwork approval (not production), a colour that has to be matched to a physical standard, and Chinese New Year. Artwork sits with the customer, so the 25–35 day clock usually starts later than people plan. We ask for the artwork at the sample stage so the two run in parallel. Shipping After Production Sea freight to the US west coast is about 30–35 days door to door; to Europe about 30–40. Express and air are possible for samples and small batches but not for 10,000 bottles. FOB Shantou is the default term; EXW and CIF are quoted on request. How to Plan a Launch Date Work backwards: retail shelf date minus 35 days freight minus 35 days production minus 10 days sample and approval. That is a 12-week runway from brief to shelf. Brands that start 8 weeks out usually pay for air freight or miss the date. The Three Queues Moulding, decoration and assembly run in sequence, and each has its own queue. A stock bottle with no decoration can leave in three weeks; a metallised cap can add ten days on its own. Artwork approval is the delay that is in the buyer's hands. A proof that comes back in two days instead of ten shortens the project more than any factory promise. Frequently Asked How long does production take? 25–35 days after sample approval for stock moulds; add 15–20 days for new tooling. How fast are samples? 7 days from an existing mould. A new shape needs the mould first, so 25–30 days in total. How long is shipping to the US or EU? About 30–35 days to the US west coast and 30–40 to Europe by sea. Can I book a slot? Yes, once the deposit is in and the artwork is approved. What about Chinese New Year? Add two to three weeks either side; the factory closes and the queue rebuilds. Still Deciding? How Do Samples Work, and What Do They Cost? Samples on stock moulds take 7 days. They are usually free; you pay the freight, collected on your account. What You Get A sample is taken from the production tool, not a showroom piece, with the closure fitted. That matters: a showroom sample that has been handled for two years tells you nothing about the tool. What It Costs Stock moulds: the sample is free, you pay freight. New tooling: the sample comes out of the trial run, which is part of the tooling cost. Before You Approve Leave the filled sample on its side for 48 hours. Most leaks show up there, not in the first hour. What a Sample Proves On a stock mould it proves the fit of your closure and the look of the pack. On a new mould, T1 proves the tool: geometry, wall and thread — not the final finish. Test it filled, with the real formula, inverted overnight. A sample that passes dry and fails wet is a thread problem, not a moulding problem. What to Write on the Approval A sentence, a photo and a date: 'approved as received, except the neck colour'. That note is what a factory can hold itself to on a repeat order, and it is the difference between a rework argument and a reorder. Frequently Asked How long do samples take? 7 days on stock moulds; longer if a new tool is needed. Can I get two colours? Yes, one sample per colour requested. Do you charge for samples? Usually not on stock moulds — you cover freight. How many rounds? One to three. More usually means the drawing was approved before it was understood. Do I pay for samples? Stock samples are normally free; T1 carries a charge that is usually credited on the first order. Still Deciding? Title: How does shipping from Shantou work? | 8PCK
Description: EXW, FOB Shantou or CIF — one 40HQ per week. A 40HQ holds roughly 20–24 pallets, depending on carton size.
Sections: The Three Terms; Container Maths; Sea, Air or Rail; What the Carton Has to Survive; What the Buyer Actually Pays; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: How does shipping from Shantou work? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / How does shipping from Shantou work? How Does Shipping From Shantou Work? EXW, FOB Shantou or CIF — one 40HQ per week. A 40HQ holds roughly 20–24 pallets, depending on carton size. The Three Terms EXW means you collect from the factory. FOB Shantou means we deliver to the port and clear export. CIF means we also pay the ocean freight to your port. Most first orders go FOB. Container Maths A 40HQ holds 20–24 pallets. The number of pieces depends on the carton: a 500 ml bottle at 28 g packs around 200 per carton, which is 40,000–48,000 per container. Sea, Air or Rail Sea from Shantou or Shenzhen is the default for bottles: 25–35 days to Europe, 30–40 to the US East Coast. Air is for samples and urgent top-ups, and costs several times more per kilo. Bottles are light for their volume, so most orders are charged on measurement rather than weight. What the Carton Has to Survive Bottles ship light and break late: the failure is almost always the carton, not the bottle. A 200-piece carton that is not full compresses in a stack, and the shoulder takes the load. Ask for the carton test: a 1.2 m drop on a corner, filled to shipping weight. If it fails, the fix is usually a divider or a smaller carton, not a thicker bottle. What the Buyer Actually Pays Three lines: ocean freight or air, the surcharges at the time of booking, and the destination charges at your end. The first is quoted, the second moves weekly, the third is the one that surprises — terminal handling and documentation at the port of arrival are not part of the freight quote. Ask the forwarder for a landed figure to your door, not a port-to-port rate. On a first order the difference between the two is usually the biggest unknown in the budget. Frequently Asked Which port? Shantou or Shenzhen, depending on the sailing. How long to Europe? 25–35 days port to port, plus customs. Can you ship LCL? Yes, for smaller volumes, with a consolidation surcharge. Which port? Shantou for full containers; Shenzhen for consolidated loads. Who handles customs? The freight forwarder, on the documents CXWN issues. Still Deciding? ## https://8pck.com/answers/verify-chinese-supplier/
Title: How do I verify a Chinese packaging supplier? | 8PCK
Description: Three checks settle it: the Unified Social Credit Code on gsxt.gov.cn, the certificate number with the issuing body, and a video call with your product in
Sections: Check 1: the Business Licence; Check 2: the Certificate Number; Check 3: the Video Call; What Each Check Rules Out; Three Checks That Take an Hour; Frequently Asked; Related
Text: How do I verify a Chinese packaging supplier? | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Answers / How do I verify a Chinese packaging supplier? How Do I Verify a Chinese Packaging Supplier? Three checks settle it: the Unified Social Credit Code on gsxt.gov.cn, the certificate number with the issuing body, and a video call with your product in hand. A supplier who cannot pass all three is a trading company with a website. Check 1: the Business Licence Every Chinese company has a Unified Social Credit Code (18 characters). Ask for it, then look it up on gsxt.gov.cn — the official register. It shows the legal name, registered capital, address and business scope. If the code does not match the name on the invoice, you are dealing with an agent, not the factory. Check 2: the Certificate Number An ISO 9001 certificate has a number and an issuing body. Call or email the body and quote the number — a real certificate is verifiable in minutes. A certificate with no number is a picture. The same applies to test reports: a laboratory report has a report number and a sample description. Check 3: the Video Call Ask for a live call walking the production line with your bottle in hand. A factory can do this in ten minutes; a trading company cannot do it at all. Ask them to show the mould number stamped on the tool — that is the thing a reseller will not have. What Each Check Rules Out The credit code rules out a fake company. The certificate number rules out a copied certificate. The video call rules out a broker. Together they are stronger than any audit report you can buy. Three Checks That Take an Hour The ISO certificate number against the issuing body, the business licence against the company name on the invoice, and a video call with the QC bench. Then one reference in your market, at your volume. A logo wall is not a reference. Frequently Asked How do I check a Chinese company? Ask for the 18-character Unified Social Credit Code and look it up on gsxt.gov.cn. How do I verify an ISO 9001 certificate? Call the certification body named on the certificate and quote the number. What if the supplier refuses a video call? That is the answer — a factory can usually do it the same day. Are audits worth it? For a first order above about USD 30,000, yes; below that, the three checks above are usually enough. Is a trading company a red flag? Not by itself — ask who makes the tool and who signs the inspection report. Should I visit? Useful, not required. A video call through the mould shop answers most of it. Still Deciding? Send the capacity, neck and quantity — we come back with a price, packing data and lead time within one business day. Title: Multi-part bottles and custom moulds | 8PCK
Description: How a four-part bottle is made and costed: part count, threads, seals, metal finishes, tooling time and confidentiality.
Sections: What "Multi-Part" Actually Means; The Three Things That Move a Mould Budget; What We Check Before the Tool Is Cut; Sealing, and How It Is Proven; Metal Finishes and One Honest Warning; Time and Confidentiality; What to Send for a Tooling Quote
Text: Multi-part bottles and custom moulds | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Custom / Multi-part bottles Custom tooling Multi-Part Bottles: When Your Pack Is Four Pieces, Not One A refill duo, a jar with a dosing insert, a tube with a collar and a decorative base — the pack is an assembly, and the mould budget follows the part count, not the bottle size. Here is how we plan it before anyone quotes. Written by Joe Joo · 8PCK, Shantou What "Multi-Part" Actually Means Most packaging quotes assume one body and one closure. When the product is designed as an assembly, each element is its own mould, its own trial and its own tolerance stack — and the tolerance stack is where a beautiful render becomes a leaking sample. Part Typical material Process What it decides Body PET, PETG, HDPE Injection or blow Holds the product; the wall carries the thread Cap or insert PETG, ABS, PP Injection Screws or sits inside the body Collar ABS, aluminium Injection or turned Carries a thread the body cannot hold Base ABS Injection Decorative; press-fit or screw Seal Silicone, EPDM Standard or moulded One per joint, in a defined groove Run the numbers before you ask a factory: mould cost estimator → The Three Things That Move a Mould Budget Part Count Four parts ≈ four times one part. Size matters less than how many separate tools you need. Thread Type A thread that can be stripped off the core is low-cost. A closed thread needs an unscrewing mechanism: +30–45 % on that part. Metal Finish Gold and chrome are applied after moulding, but they need jigs and masking — and they change how the part is handled. What We Check Before the Tool Is Cut Wall and draft. PETG at 2.5 mm is a slow cycle; 1.8 mm usually looks the same on shelf and costs less. Seal groove. An O-ring needs a defined groove depth and squeeze; a flat gasket needs a land width. Two threads on one joint. If both sides turn the same way, opening the cap can unscrew the body — one side goes left-hand. Through-bore or divider. A chamber that must stay separate until use needs a plug, a membrane or a valve — decide before tooling. Gate position. On a clear part, the gate shows. It goes at the base or under the collar, never on the shoulder. Sealing, and How It Is Proven We ask for the test, not just the word "airtight": vacuum hold (for example −0.3 bar for 30 seconds), a shake test with the real formula, or a drop test to the retail standard. The seal material follows the chemistry — silicone for most emulsions, EPDM where a solvent is involved. Metal Finishes and One Honest Warning Vacuum metallising gives the champagne-gold look on ABS at a moderate cost; electroplating is harder wearing and two to three times the price. Either can be attacked by an acid peel or a high-alcohol formula, so we ask for the pH and the solvent before the finish is chosen. If the formula is aggressive, the plated part moves to the outside and a PP liner goes inside. Time and Confidentiality Drawing review — 3–5 days, with a DFM note back to you. Tooling — 30–40 days for a four-part assembly. T1 samples — 7–10 days, sent for fit and leak test. Production — 30–35 days after approval. Your drawing stays yours. We sign an NDA before files are shared, we do not reuse a customer's tool for anyone else, and uploaded files are deleted on request — usually within 30 days. part 1 part 2 collar part 3 seal seal seal Generic assembly diagram — placeholder shapes, not any customer part. No — we supply the case and mechanism; filling stays with the cosmetics manufacturer. How We Quote and Ship Send capacity, neck, quantity and the closure you intend to use. Title: Soft tubes — 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300 ml | 8PCK
Description: A tube is the cheapest way to put a cream, gel or paste on a shelf — and the format most often specified without deciding whether the product needs an EVOH
Sections: When a Barrier Layer Earns Its Cost; Print Before Filling, Always; What to Send With the Brief; Questions We Get on This Format
Text: Soft tubes — 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300 ml | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Formats / Soft tubes Format Soft Tubes: 30–300 ml, Barrier Layers and What Print Does to Lead Time By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 2026 A tube is the cheapest way to put a cream, gel or paste on a shelf — and the format most often specified without deciding whether the product needs an EVOH barrier. Extruded tubes are made in the same building as our bottles: the tube body is extruded, the shoulder and cap are injection moulded, and the print goes on before filling. This page covers the sizes we run, when a barrier layer earns its cost, and how decoration changes the schedule. When a Barrier Layer Earns Its Cost An EVOH layer slows oxygen and aroma transfer. It matters for essential oils, vitamin C, and anything with a fragrance that has to survive twelve months on a shelf. It roughly doubles the tube's material cost. For a body lotion in a 200 ml tube, mono PE is usually enough; for a 30 ml serum, the barrier is what keeps the formula from turning. Print Before Filling, Always Tubes are printed as blanks, then filled and sealed at the cap end. That means artwork approval comes before production, and a late change stops the line rather than delaying a label. Six-colour offset or flexo is standard; hot stamp and metallising are available at 5,000 pcs. What to Send With the Brief Fill volume, product viscosity, whether the formula contains a solvent, cap style, and the artwork. Viscosity decides the orifice; the solvent decides whether the inner layer needs to change. Samples from an existing tube mould leave in 7 days; a new diameter needs a die, which is 15–20 days. Questions We Get on This Format What is the minimum order for a printed tube? 3,000 pcs per design at 1–6 colours. Below that, plain tubes with a label are the practical route. Can the tube be refilled? Not practically — the seal at the crimp end is single-use. Tubes are priced as single-use packs. Do you supply the cap and the tube together? Yes. Flip-top, screw and octagonal caps are moulded in the same plant and fitted before packing. At a glance Sizes 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300 ml Tube diameter Ø 19–50 mm Material PE mono, PE + EVOH barrier Caps Flip-top, screw, octagonal, flat-top Printing 1–6 colours, matt or gloss varnish MOQ 3,000 pcs per design Lead time 30–40 days after artwork approval Ask About This Format → Written quotation, lead time and a sample plan in one reply. ## https://8pck.com/formats/straw-fibre-bottles/
Title: Straw-fibre bottles — 100, 200, 250, 300, 500 ml | 8PCK
Description: Wheat-straw HDPE is not biodegradable. It is HDPE with 20–30 % agricultural fibre, which changes the colour, the surface and the story — not the recycling
Sections: What It Is, in One Paragraph; Where the Fibre Shows; Claims That Survive an Audit; Questions We Get on This Format
Text: Straw-fibre bottles — 100, 200, 250, 300, 500 ml | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Formats / Straw-fibre bottles Format Straw-Fibre Bottles: What Wheat Straw Actually Adds to HDPE By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 2026 Wheat-straw HDPE is not biodegradable. It is HDPE with 20–30 % agricultural fibre, which changes the colour, the surface and the story — not the recycling stream. Buyers ask for “eco bottles” and often mean three different things: recycled content, a bio-based filler, or a compostable material. Straw-fibre HDPE is the second one. This page is explicit about what it does and does not claim, because a wrong environmental claim is worse than no claim. What It Is, in One Paragraph Wheat straw is dried, milled and compounded into HDPE. The result is a mouldable plastic with a visible fibre speckle and a lower carbon footprint per kilo than virgin HDPE — but it is still HDPE, and it still goes into the same recycling stream as HDPE. It is not biodegradable, not compostable, and not food-contact certified by default. Say so on the pack, or a retailer will ask you to. Where the Fibre Shows Natural is the honest colour: a light beige with visible flecks. White and green use masterbatch to cover it, which reduces the “natural” story to a texture rather than a colour. The surface is matte and slightly textured, which hides scratches — a practical advantage for a bottle that travels. Claims That Survive an Audit Safe: “contains 25 % wheat-straw fibre”, “bio-based filler”, “lower-carbon material”. Unsafe: “biodegradable”, “plastic-free”, “compostable”. The first three are true; the last three are not. Ask for the compound supplier's declaration before printing anything on the bottle. Questions We Get on This Format Is straw-fibre plastic biodegradable? No. It is HDPE with a bio-based filler; it behaves like HDPE in recycling and in landfill. Can it be used for food contact? Only with a food-contact declaration for the specific compound. We ask for it per order rather than assume. Does it cost more than standard HDPE? Yes — typically 15–25 % more, driven by the compound rather than the moulding. At a glance Sizes 100, 200, 250, 300, 500 ml Material HDPE + 20–30 % wheat straw fibre Colour Natural, white, green — no added masterbatch in natural Surface Matte, slightly fibrous; takes silkscreen well MOQ 1,000 pcs per colour Lead time 25–35 days after sample approval Ask About This Format → Written quotation, lead time and a sample plan in one reply. ## https://8pck.com/glossary/
Title: Plastic packaging glossary — 24 terms explained | 8PCK
Description: Neck finish, MOQ, preform, airless, mass balance and 19 more packaging terms, defined in plain English.
Text: Plastic packaging glossary — 24 terms explained | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Glossary Glossary Plastic Packaging Terms, in Plain English The words buyers and suppliers use differently — and what each one actually means on a drawing. Neck Finish The opening specification, written as diameter/thread — e.g. 24/410 is 24 mm diameter with a 410 thread profile. Read more → MOQ Minimum order quantity. At 8PCK it is 1,000 pcs per colour on existing moulds. Read more → Blow Mould The tool that forms a bottle. About USD 850 and 15–20 days at CXWN, and it belongs to the customer. Read more → Preform The test-tube-shaped PET piece that is stretch-blown into a bottle. Read more → Airless A pack with a piston and no dip tube, so the product never meets air. Read more → Dropper A pipette closure on an 18/410 neck, used for serums and oils. Read more → Lotion Pump A pump that dispenses 1.2–2.0 ml per stroke; the default closure for 250–500 ml bottles. Read more → Foam Pump A pump that mixes air with a low-viscosity formula at the nozzle to produce foam. Read more → Trigger Sprayer A hand-squeezed sprayer on a 28/410 neck, used for home care and garden. Read more → Disc-Top Cap A cap that opens on a hinge with a small orifice; the lowest unit cost controlled-flow closure. Read more → Induction Seal A foil liner sealed to a jar rim by heat; it needs a flat land on the rim. Read more → EPE Liner A foam liner inside a screw cap. low-cost and fine for dry goods and creams; swells with oils. Read more → Sleeve A shrink film wrapped around a bottle. Makes PET harder to recycle. Read more → Silkscreen Direct printing on the bottle; from 1,000 pcs, and the most durable decoration for a wet environment. Read more → Spray Coat A painted finish on a bottle; from 3,000 pcs and adds 5–8 days. Read more → Hot Stamp Foil stamping for a metallic look; from 3,000 pcs. Read more → PET Polyethylene terephthalate — clear, stiff, widely recycled; poor with strong solvents. Read more → HDPE High-density polyethylene — opaque, tough, low-cost, good with surfactants. Read more → LDPE Low-density polyethylene — soft and squeezable, used for sauce and gel bottles. Read more → PETG A thicker-walled clear plastic that reads closer to glass than PET. Read more → PP Polypropylene — the material for hot fill above 60 °C and for most closures. Read more → Mass Balance An accounting method for recycled content; not the same as physically recycled content. Read more → AQL Acceptable quality limit — the sampling standard used at inspection. Flip-Top lower in unit cost, used for refill formats and value lines. The Wall Has to Hold A full 750 ml at 0.55 mm flexes under a stroke and the pump draws air. 0.65 mm at the shoulder is the practical floor, and 0.7 mm for a rough handling chain. Export Economics A 750 ml carton is heavy: check pallet weight limits before fixing the pack count. Freight per litre drops, but the case can hit a limit a 500 ml case does not. Where This Size Fails At 750 ml the pack is a container before it is a brand object. Failures come from the shoulder, the base and the closure — in that order. Shoulder Flex A full bottle puts load on the shoulder; below 0.65 mm a pump stroke deforms it and draws air. Base Sag A flat, reinforced base is needed or cases sag in a pallet stack over weeks. Closure Mismatch 38 mm and 38-400 are not the same specification; confirm the thread on the drawing. What to Send in a Brief Capacity (750 ml), product type, neck, closure, and whether the pack ships as a retail unit or a refill. Clear PET for a product that has to be seen; HDPE where the formula is opaque or attacks PET; PETG when the wall has to look thick like glass. 500 ml and 1 L bracket it — the neck is usually shared, which is why one closure range covers the whole family. If you are switching between 750 ml and 1 L, keep the neck the same and only the body changes. Clear PET The default for shampoo, water and anything sold on colour; light, recyclable, food-grade. HDPE Opaque, cheap, and resistant to surfactants — the choice for detergent and chemicals. PETG Thicker wall, closer to glass; costs 20–30 % more per unit. ## https://8pck.com/guides/airless-bottles/
Title: Airless Bottles — specs, MOQ and documents | 8PCK
Description: An airless bottle has no dip tube. A piston follows the product down, so the formula meets air only at the nozzle. That protects actives — and costs more t
Sections: How an Airless Pack Actually Works; When Airless Is Worth It; Airless vs Dropper vs Standard Pump; What to Specify Before Quoting; Where Airless Disappoints; How to Specify One; Questions We Get on This; Sizes That Fit This Guide
Text: Airless Bottles — specs, MOQ and documents | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Guides / Airless Bottles Guide Airless Bottles: How They Work, and When They Are Worth the Cost By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 26 October 2026 An airless bottle has no dip tube. A piston follows the product down, so the formula meets air only at the nozzle. That protects actives — and costs more than a standard pump bottle. Here is when it earns the difference. Airless packaging solves a specific problem: oxidation and contamination of a formula that is expensive enough to protect. Vitamin C, retinol, foundation, sun care — the products where the last 10% of the bottle still has to perform. We mould the bottle and supply a matched airless pump, tested as a set rather than assembled from two suppliers' parts. Check it before you quote The free Bottle Spec Checker tests whether your neck fits the closure and whether the wall survives a pump stroke. 30-second check: does your bottle pass? Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — How an Airless Pack Actually Works A standard pump bottle has a dip tube reaching the bottom; the pump pulls liquid up and air comes in to replace it. An airless pack has no tube. The pump sits on top of the product and a piston at the base rises as product leaves, so the chamber shrinks and no air enters. Two consequences follow: the formula is protected from oxidation, and the pack can dispense almost completely — typically over 95% of the fill, against 70–80% for a dip-tube bottle. When Airless Is Worth It Worth it: actives that oxidise, products where the dose matters (foundation, serum), preservative-free formulations, and premium positioning where the pack is part of the price story. Not worth it: water-thin toners, products with large particles that clog the valve, and any project where a 24/410 pump bottle achieves the same result at two-thirds the cost. Airless vs Dropper vs Standard Pump A dropper is the lowest unit cost way to dispense a precise small dose of oil or serum, and the least protective. A standard pump is the workhorse for lotions and washes. Airless sits at the top on protection and unit cost, and is the right answer only when the formula justifies it. What to Specify Before Quoting Four numbers decide the quote: capacity, dose per stroke, fill volume as a percentage, and the decoration. Get those four right and the pump can be matched to the formula's viscosity without sampling twice. Where Airless Disappoints Airless is the right answer less often than the category suggests. Three cases where it is not. Thin, Water-Like Formulas A toner or micellar water does not oxidise in a dip-tube bottle. Paying 30-50 % more for airless buys nothing the formula needs. Formulas With Particles Scrubs, glitters and some serums clog the piston valve. A standard pump with a wider orifice handles them better. Launches Under 3,000 pcs Thick-wall PETG and a matched piston pump start at 3,000. At 1,000 the per-unit premium is often 2×, which kills the business case. How to Specify One Four numbers decide the quote: capacity, dose per stroke, fill volume as a percentage of nominal, and decoration. Get those right and the pump can be matched to viscosity without a second sampling round. For a 30 ml serum, 0.10-0.15 ml per stroke is typical; for a 50 ml foundation, 0.20-0.25 ml. Questions We Get on This Can an airless bottle be refilled? Not practically. The piston and pump are a sealed set; refilling risks contamination. Treat it as a single-use pack and price it that way. Can you print on an airless bottle? Yes — silkscreen and hot stamp on the body, and spray coat or soft-touch as a base finish. Metallising is available at 3,000 pcs MOQ. What is the MOQ for a custom airless pack? 1,000 pcs per colour on the 30 ml and 50 ml moulds we hold. A new shape starts at 3,000–5,000 pcs.

That single fact decides the bottle: the closure, the grip and the label, in that order — the volume is almost an afterthought. Body wash and shower gel move in 250, 400, 500 and 750 ml, in clear PET or opaque HDPE. Almost every complaint is about the pack, not the product: a pump that slips, a bottle that is hard to grip, a label that peels in a wet bathroom. This page covers the sizes we mould, which closure suits which habit, and what to specify so the pack survives twelve showers a week. Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — The Closure Is the Product A disc-top is lowest unit cost and works with one hand; a lotion pump doses more precisely but needs a firmer grip; a flip-top is the compromise most brands land on for 500 ml. A pump that works with dry hands in a showroom can slip in a shower — the fix is usually a larger actuator, not a different pump. 500 ml Is a Habit, Not a Standard In the US and UK, 500 ml is the default body wash size; in Germany and the Nordics, 250–300 ml sells alongside it as a “try” size; in Southeast Asia, 400 ml is common because of shelf price points. What a Wet Bathroom Does to a Label Paper labels wrinkle; standard permanent adhesive lifts at the edges after a few weeks of steam. For a body wash that lives in the shower, specify a synthetic label with a waterproof adhesive, or print directly on the bottle. Silkscreen is the most durable option and the lowest unit cost at 1,000 pcs — the trade-off is colour count and artwork complexity. PET or HDPE for Body Wash Clear PET shows the gel colour and reads premium; HDPE is opaque, it costs less per gram and hides the fill level as the bottle empties. Most value lines choose HDPE, most masstige lines choose PET. If the gel contains exfoliating particles, a wider neck (28/410) makes filling faster and reduces clogging at the pump. Where Body Wash Bottles Fail The bathroom is a hostile environment for packaging. Three failures dominate. Steam and Labels A body wash bottle sits in a shower for months. Synthetic label plus waterproof adhesive, or silkscreen; paper will lift at the edges. Gel Viscosity vs Pump A thick gel needs a wider dip tube and a larger valve, or the pump feels stiff and doses unevenly. Bottle Falls in the Shower A 500 ml full bottle dropped from waist height lands on the shoulder. A 0.55 mm wall handles it; a 0.45 mm wall cracks. 400 ml in Southeast Asia, 500 ml in the US Shelf price points decide the size, not the formula. 400 ml is common in Southeast Asia where the entry price matters; 500 ml is the US and UK default; 250 ml sits alongside as a travel or trial size. One mould family can serve all three, which is why a 500 ml mould with two smaller derivatives is the usual production setup. Which closure should I choose for body wash? Disc-top for one-handed use and lowest cost; flip-top for a balance; lotion pump for a premium dose. Test all three with wet hands before deciding. Four processes, what each costs in MOQ and lead time, and how to choose between them. The bottle is the same; the decoration is the difference between a 40-cent pack and a 90-cent pack at retail. It is also the step where buyers discover that four-colour print has a different minimum from one-colour. Here is what each process actually requires, in numbers. Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — Silkscreen: the Workhorse One to four colours, applied directly to the bottle. It is the lowest unit cost way to put a logo on a pack and the most forgiving on small runs — 1,000 pcs, five extra days. Limitation: it prints on curved surfaces in straight lines. Complex gradients and photographs are not silkscreen work; those go to labels or sleeves. Hot Stamp and Spray Coat: the Premium Two Hot stamping presses foil into the surface for a metallic logo. Spray coating covers the whole bottle in matte, gloss or soft-touch. Both need 3,000 pcs because both are set-up-heavy: plates, masking, oven time. Soft-touch is the finish that most often sells a premium line, and the one that shows fingerprints. Say so to your customer before they approve it. Labels Are Not a Downgrade A pressure-sensitive label on a clear bottle can carry full-colour artwork and variable data that silkscreen cannot, at 1,000 pcs and three extra days. For short runs and market tests, it is usually the right first move — then switch to print once the design stops changing. Artwork: What We Need to Quote Vector artwork (AI or PDF) with the print area marked, the Pantone references, and the bottle drawing. Without the print area, every supplier quotes a different price for a different amount of ink. Choosing Decoration by Volume Decoration is where a stock bottle becomes a brand, and where MOQ jumps. The decision is volume first. Under 1,000 pcs Digital label or a stock-colour bottle with a printed label. Silkscreen plates are not economic; spray coat is not available. 1,000–3,000 pcs Silkscreen in one to four colours. This is the sweet spot: a plate is a one-off, and four colours still print in one pass. Above 3,000 pcs Spray coat, hot stamp, metallising. Each adds 5-10 days and a set-up cost, and each reads as premium on shelf. What Decoration Does to Recycling A full-body sleeve makes a PET bottle unrecyclable in practice; a paper label with wash-off adhesive keeps it in the stream. If the brand makes a recyclability claim, the decoration is part of the claim. Questions We Get on This What is the lowest unit cost way to brand a bottle? One-colour silkscreen at 1,000 pcs. It is also the fastest, adding about five days to production. Can I mix decoration methods on one order? Yes, but each method has its own MOQ and its own set-up. A 1,000 pc silkscreen plus 3,000 pc hot stamp means the hot stamp runs at 3,000. Do you print on the cap as well? Yes — silkscreen or hot stamp on caps, quoted separately from the bottle. Can you match a Pantone colour exactly? We match to the Pantone reference on the bottle material, which shifts slightly on coloured resin. A physical sample is the only reliable approval. What is the cheapest decoration? A label on a stock-colour bottle below 1,000 pcs; silkscreen above 1,000. How many colours can be silkscreened? Text: Bottle Neck Finishes — specs, MOQ and documents | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Guides / Bottle Neck Finishes Guide Bottle Neck Finishes: 18/410, 20/410, 24/410 and 28/410 Explained By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 26 October 2026 The neck finish decides which pump, cap or sprayer fits your bottle. It is also the number buyers most often leave out of a brief — and the reason a container of pumps arrives that nobody can use. Every bottle we mould is defined by its neck before anything else. The neck is the only part of the container that has to interface with a component made somewhere else, to a tolerance measured in tenths of a millimetre. Below is how the four finishes we hold in stock are used, and how to choose between them. Check it before you quote The free Bottle Spec Checker tests whether your neck fits the closure and whether the wall survives a pump stroke. 30-second check: does your bottle pass? Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — What the Two Numbers Mean Take 24/410. The 24 is the nominal outside diameter of the neck in millimetres. The 410 is the thread standard: a single-start thread with a defined pitch and depth. Two bottles can both be “24 mm” and still take different closures if the thread differs — which is why the second number is the one to quote. Why the Same Neck From Two Suppliers May Not Fit Thread dimensions have a tolerance band, and moulds wear. A pump that clicks onto one 24/410 bottle may feel tight on another. This is normal and is why we test pumps on our own bottles rather than trusting the drawing alone. If you are buying bottles and pumps from different suppliers, ask both for the neck drawing and compare the thread callout, not just the diameter. Matching a Closure to a Product Viscous products — lotions, creams, gels — need a pump with a dip tube that reaches the bottom corner. Thin products suit a disc-top or flip-top. Oils and serums usually take a dropper at 18/410. Mist sprayers at 20/410 and 24/410 are for fragrances and toners. Where Neck Specs Go Wrong The failures are consistent, and all of them are visible on a sample within a week. Mixing 410 and 415 Threads Both are 24 mm, both accept a 24 mm pump, and only one seals. A 24/415 bottle with a 24/410 pump threads on by hand and leaks on a filling line at 2 bar. Ask the closure supplier for the thread code, not just the diameter. Measuring the Neck on a Photo Neck finish cannot be read from a product photo — the thread height is 2.5 mm on a 410 and 5 mm on a 415. Send a bottle, or a caliper reading of T, E and H dimensions. Assuming a Neck Is Standard Because the Bottle Is A 500 ml bottle shape is often available with two different necks from the same mould family. Confirm the neck on the drawing, not on the model name. What to Send in a Brief The complete neck code (e.g. 24/410), the closure you intend to use, and one sample if you have it. With those three we confirm fit before quoting, instead of after the first container. If you are choosing the neck as well, 24/410 covers most pumps; 28/410 for 500-750 ml; 18/410 and 20/410 for droppers and mist sprayers. Questions We Get on This Is 24/410 the same as 24/415? No. Both are 24 mm necks, but the thread differs and closures are not interchangeable. Quote the full number, including the thread, on every purchase order. Can you make a bottle with a neck you do not stock? Yes, with a new neck insert. It is a modification to an existing mould rather than a new mould, typically USD 300–800 and 7–10 days. How do I measure a neck without a drawing? Measure the outside diameter across the threads with a caliper, then send a photo of the closure's thread. We identify the finish from those two. Text: How to Choose a Plastic Bottle Manufacturer in China | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Guides / Choosing a Manufacturer Guide How to Choose a Plastic Bottle Manufacturer in China — 2026 Checklist By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 26 October 2026 Most buyers shortlist on price and a website. The factories that ship on time are separated by seven questions that take ten minutes to ask — and almost nobody asks them before sending a deposit. There are thousands of companies in China that will quote a plastic bottle. A minority of them own the mould, blow the bottle, make the pump and print it in the same building. The difference shows up in your third order, not the first. This checklist is what we would ask if we were buying — including the questions that are uncomfortable for a supplier. Check it before you quote The free Bottle Spec Checker tests whether your neck fits the closure and whether the wall survives a pump stroke. 30-second check: does your bottle pass? Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — 1. Is It a Factory or a Trading Company Both are legitimate, but they fail differently. A trading company adds a margin and loses control of the schedule; a factory that claims to be a factory usually cannot show you the mould shop. Ask for the business licence and the factory address, then check that the scope of business includes plastic products manufacturing. A licence registered to an office address with a trading scope is not a factory. 2. Who Owns the Mould This is the single most important question in custom packaging. If the factory owns the mould, you are renting capacity; if you own it, you can move the tool. A new blow mould costs from USD 850 — small enough that ownership should be negotiated in writing, not assumed. Ask: who holds the tool, where is it stored, and what happens to it if we stop ordering? 3. Does the Pump Come From the Same Building Bottle, neck and pump are three parts with three tolerances. When the pump comes from a different supplier, the leak is discovered by your customer. A factory that moulds both tests the assembly as one unit. If they do not make pumps, ask which pump brand they fit and whether they will test your pump on their bottle. 4. Can They Verify the Certificate Anyone can put an ISO logo on a page. A real supplier gives you the certificate number, the issuing body and the scope — enough for you to check it independently. Ours is ISO 9001:2015, certificate PCC85721Q00018R0S, issued by ProCision Shanghai. Be equally suspicious of a full set of badges (FDA, REACH, GRS, BRC) on a site that cannot produce a single scan. 5. What Does the Sample Prove A sample pulled from a showroom shelf proves nothing about production. Ask for a sample from the actual production mould, with the batch record, and weigh it: a bottle that is 2 g under spec is a bottle that will collapse under a pump stroke. 6. What the Quote Must Contain A unit price alone is not a quote. You need the packing configuration (carton quantity, pallet, container load), the lead time from deposit, the incoterm, and what is excluded — decoration, mould, sampling, testing. If the packing data is missing, you cannot calculate freight, and the lowest unit cost quote often becomes the most expensive order. 7. Red Flags Worth Walking Away From A price 30% below everyone else with no explanation. A supplier who will not put the mould ownership in writing. A sample that arrives without a batch record. A certificate that cannot be verified. And a supplier who answers every technical question with “no problem” — because the answer to a wall thickness question is a number, not a promise. The Five Checks That Actually Predict a Good Supplier Price is the last thing to compare, not the first. These five separate factories that will still be there in three years. This page covers fill weight, single versus double wall, and how the cap decides the feel. Cosmetic jars are sold by fill weight: 30 g, 50 g, 100 g. The number tells you how much product goes in, not how big the jar is. A 30 g jar in single-wall PET and a 30 g jar in double-wall PETG hold the same amount and read as two different price points. That gap — same fill, different perceived value — is the whole game in skincare packaging. Check it before you quote The free Bottle Spec Checker tests whether your neck fits the closure and whether the wall survives a pump stroke. 30-second check: does your bottle pass? Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — Single Wall vs Double Wall A single-wall jar is one moulded piece: lighter, costs less, and is the standard for volume skincare. A double-wall jar has an outer shell and a separate inner cup, so the product never touches the decorated surface and the wall can be thick without using more resin than necessary. Double wall is what makes a jar feel expensive. It is also what makes it heavier to ship, and the two parts have to be assembled — both of which show up in the unit price. Why the Cap Decides the Feel Buyers judge a jar by the lid: the sound it makes and the weight in the hand. A thin PP cap on a thick-wall jar feels wrong immediately. For premium lines the cap is often the heavier part — ABS or thick PP, sometimes with a metal-look insert. If you are sampling, judge the jar with its cap on. Half the perceived quality is in the closure. Threads, Refills and the EU Refill Push A screw jar can be refilled only if the refill cup is designed for it; most double-wall jars are not. If refillability is part of the claim, say so at the brief stage — it changes both the mould and the packaging configuration. Where Cosmetic Jars Leak, and It Is Usually the Liner A cream jar that leaks in transit is rarely a mould problem. Three causes cover most of it. Liner Incompatible With the Formula Oil-based creams swell EPE liners; silicone liners cost more and resist. If the formula has a high oil phase, specify the liner with the jar. Over-Torque at the Filling Line A torque above the jar's spec distorts the liner and opens a gap on one side. Specify a torque range with the capping machine, not a 'tight' instruction. Thread Depth on a Double-Wall Jar Double-wall jars have an inner cup; the thread is on the outer shell. A liner that fits a single-wall jar may not sit flat on a double-wall rim. Frosting, Spray Coat and What They Cost Frosting is a surface treatment from 1,000 pcs and reads as soft-touch glass. Spray coat and metallising start at 3,000 and add 5-8 days. For a 30 g cream at launch volume, frosting plus label is usually the cheapest premium look. Questions We Get on This Is a 30 g jar the same as a 30 ml jar? Not exactly. Grams measure fill weight, millilitres measure volume. A 30 g cream at typical density is close to 30 ml, but a light emulsion can be 35 ml in the same jar. Can you print on a jar lid? Yes — silkscreen or hot stamp on the lid top, at 1,000 and 3,000 pcs MOQ respectively. What is the MOQ for a frosted jar? 1,000 pcs. Frosting is a surface treatment, not a colour, so it does not add a colour changeover. Can the jar be made from recycled material? PET and PETG can include recycled content; the percentage changes clarity and needs its own declaration. Ask for the grade before you promise a recycled claim. What is a standard cosmetic jar size? 30 g, 50 g and 100 g by fill weigh

Sections: Part Count Beats Part Size; The Band, by Part Size; The Unscrewing Penalty; Finish, Seal and the Hidden Allowances; What a Four-Part Assembly Looks Like in Numbers; Why Two Factories Quote 3× Apart; Where the Days Go After T1; What We Need Before the Number Is Firm
Text: What a custom bottle mould costs, part by part | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Guides / What a Custom Bottle Mould Costs, Part by Part | 8PCK Guide What a Custom Bottle Mould Costs, Part by Part By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 31 October 2026 A four-part pack is not four times a one-part pack by accident. Here is where the money goes, why a thread can add 40 %, and what the number looks like before a drawing exists. Every enquiry that starts with a drawing eventually asks the same question: what will the tooling cost? The honest answer depends on four things, and only one of them is the size of the bottle. This page sets out how we price a mould before we cut steel: the band per part, the multipliers that move it, and the place where a low-cost mould becomes an expensive year. Check it before you quote The free Bottle Spec Checker tests whether your neck fits the closure and whether the wall survives a pump stroke. 30-second check: does your bottle pass? Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — Part Count Beats Part Size One body and one cap is a two-mould project. A refill duo, a jar with a dosing insert, or a serum with a collar and a base is four or five. Each part carries its own tool, its own trial and its own tolerance stack, so the budget scales with the count first. That is why a 30 ml dropper bottle can cost more to tool than a 500 ml shampoo bottle: the small one has a body, a collar, a pipette and a cap; the large one has a body and a closure. The Band, by Part Size Small parts — under 50 ml, under 60 mm across — usually sit between USD 1,800 and 3,500 with one cavity. Medium parts, the 50–250 ml band at 60–80 mm, run 3,000 to 6,000. Large parts, or anything with a thick wall and a long cycle, start at 4,500 and reach 9,000. Cavities multiply rather than add: two cavities are about 1.6 times the single-cavity tool, four cavities about 2.6 times. Below 20,000 pieces a year, one cavity is almost always the right purchase. The Unscrewing Penalty A thread on the outside of a neck can be stripped off the core as the part ejects. A thread on the inside of a cap cannot: the core has to rotate out, which means a mechanism, a slower cycle and a more expensive tool. That single decision adds 30 to 45 % to the affected part. It is also why a two-piece cap — a shell plus a threaded insert — sometimes costs less than a one-piece lid, even though it is an extra mould and an extra assembly step. Finish, Seal and the Hidden Allowances Metal finishes are applied after moulding, but they need jigs and masking, which adds roughly USD 250–700 per part. An O-ring groove is free to design and expensive to get wrong: too shallow and the ring is crushed, too deep and it never seals. A flat gasket needs a land width and a flatness callout that a blow-moulded body cannot hold. This is where a two-hundred-dollar saving on tooling turns into a leak test that fails at the filling line. What a Four-Part Assembly Looks Like in Numbers Take a 200 ml pack: a body, an upper section, a collar and a decorative base, all medium parts, one cavity each, with a vacuum-metallised finish on two of them. The band lands near USD 15,000–19,000, and the same parts at two cavities head towards 26,000. Spread over 5,000 sets, that is roughly USD 3.00–3.80 of tooling per set; over 20,000 sets it falls under a dollar. The tool does not get lower in unit cost — the order gets bigger. Why Two Factories Quote 3× Apart A USD 4,000 tool and a USD 12,000 tool can both produce a first sample that looks right. The difference appears at month nine: steel grade, heat treatment, polishing and the number of trial shots the price includes. low-cost tools are usually cut from softer steel with fewer slides. They run fine for 30,000 shots and start flashing at 80,000. If the product is a one-season launch, that is a rational trad

Text: Dropper Bottles — specs, MOQ and documents | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Guides / Dropper Bottles Guide Dropper Bottles: 18/410, Glass vs Plastic, and Dose per Drop By Joe Joo · 8PCK · Shantou · Updated 26 October 2026 A dropper bottle is a bottle, a collar and a pipette that have to seal at three points. The 18/410 neck is the standard for serums and oils — the rest is a choice between glass weight and plastic economics. Serums, oils and tinctures are dosed by the drop, which makes the dropper the product experience rather than a closure. A pipette that drips two drops when the label says one is a complaint waiting to happen. We supply 18/410 bottles in PET with glass or plastic droppers, and test the assembly as a unit. Check it before you quote The free Bottle Spec Checker tests whether your neck fits the closure and whether the wall survives a pump stroke. 30-second check: does your bottle pass? Open ▾ Capacity (ml) Wall (mm) Closure Lotion pump Sprayer Flip-top Dropper Screw cap Full Check → — Glass vs Plastic Glass reads premium and is inert — the right choice for essential oils and anything with a solvent. It is also heavier, breaks, and costs more to ship. PET reads clean and modern, weighs a third as much, and is the pragmatic choice for e-liquid, travel sizes and sample kits. The dropper itself can still be glass in a PET bottle. Why the Collar Matters More Than the Bottle The collar holds the pipette and seals against the neck. If it is loose, the product leaks into the cap; if it is over-tight, the pipette cracks. This is the part we test on every batch rather than sampling. Dose per Drop Is a Specification, Not a Guess Drop size depends on the bore of the pipette and the viscosity of the liquid. Water-like serums give about 0.05 ml per drop; oils give less. If your label says “3 drops”, test with the actual fill before printing the carton. Where Dropper Bottles Go Wrong Four failures, all visible on a filled sample within a week. The Pipette Does Not Reach the Base A tube 5 mm short leaves the last 3 ml unusable. It is a length decision made at assembly, not a mould decision, and it is the most common complaint. Bulb Perishes Rubber bulbs harden and crack after a few hundred uses, especially with essential oils. A push-button dropper costs 20-30 % more and removes the problem. Glass Pipette in a Plastic Bottle The compromise most brands use: glass for the premium feel, PET for the freight. Check the collar fit — an 18/410 collar on a 18/415 neck leaks. Label Over the Neck A label that wraps the shoulder interferes with the collar. Keep the label 8 mm below the neck. Sizing a Serum Bottle 15 ml for trial, 30 ml for the standard serum, 50 ml for body serum and hair oil. The 30 ml is the volume that fits a four-to-six-week routine, which is why it dominates. Questions We Get on This Can you supply the dropper separately? Yes — 18/410 droppers at 1,000 pcs MOQ, glass or plastic, whether or not you buy the bottle from us. Is a 30 ml dropper bottle really 30 ml? Nominal capacity is to the shoulder, not the brim. With the dropper inserted, usable fill is typically 25–28 ml — plan the label claim accordingly. Do you offer child-resistant droppers? Yes, in 18/410 for CBD and essential oil markets where the destination market requires it. Push-button dropper: what it is and when it pays ['A push-button dropper replaces the rubber bulb with a button on top: press, the pipette fills, release, the dose stays. It costs roughly 20–30 % more than a bulb dropper but removes the two complaints that come with bulbs — inconsistent dose and the bulb perishing after a few hundred uses.', 'It suits actives sold on precision (retinol, peptides) and markets where the pack is handled by untrained staff. For a 30 ml serum at 1,000 pcs, the difference is usually a few cents per unit.'] Can the pipette be printed with a logo? On the bulb or the collar, ye
