Text: Bottles — PET · HDPE · PETG | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Products / Bottles PET · HDPE · PETG Bottles, and Why Weight, Not Shape, Sets the Price 50–1,000 ml, 18–38 mm necks. Eight stock moulds, ready for decoration. 8 SKU Capacity All 50 100 250 500 Material All PET HDPE PETG Neck All 20/410 24/410 28/410 500 ml PET Pump Bottle 24/410 · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 250 ml PET Pump Bottle 24/410 · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 300 ml PET Pump Bottle 24/410 · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 750 ml Shampoo Bottle 28/410 · HDPE MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 100 ml PET Round Bottle 20/410 · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 200 ml Flat Bottle 24/410 · HDPE MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 50 ml Travel Bottle 20/410 · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 30 ml PET Dropper Bottle 18/410 · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → What Buyers Get Wrong Choosing the Neck Before the Pump The pump is usually already specified by the brand's filler. Send the closure first; the neck follows it, not the other way round. Cutting Weight After the Sample Two grams off the shoulder to save freight is enough to make a pump draw air. Re-test if the weight changes. Assuming a Clear Bottle Is PETG Clear PET and PETG look identical in a photo and differ 20–30 % in price. Ask which resin the quote uses. What We Mould, and in Which Material Bottles run from 50 ml to 750 ml in three materials. PET is clear and stiff, and takes a pump without flexing: the default for shampoo, hand soap and body wash where the product has to be seen. HDPE is opaque and it costs less per gram, and hides the fill level as the bottle empties, which is why value and professional lines use it. PETG sits between: clearer and thicker-walled than HDPE, and the usual choice for premium thick-wall cosmetic bottles. The size is usually a market decision before it is a design one. 500 ml is the retail standard in the US and UK; 250-300 ml sells in Germany and the Nordics; 400 ml is common in Southeast Asia where shelf price points are lower. The Neck Is the Specification That Matters A 24/410 bottle does not take a 28/410 pump. If you already buy closures, send one and we test it on the bottle before quoting. If you are choosing both, 24/410 covers most lotion and soap lines, and 28/410 is for larger pumps on 500-750 ml bottles. Wall thickness follows the pump: a full stroke pushes down on the shoulder, so a bottle under 0.55 mm can flex and draw air. We quote the wall with the mould, not after the sample. Decoration, and What It Costs in MOQ Silkscreen in one to four colours starts at 1,000 pcs and adds about five days. Labels are lower in unit cost for multi-colour artwork and allow short runs. Hot stamp and spray coat start at 3,000 pcs because both are set-up heavy. A stock bottle with a good silkscreen reads as bespoke at a fraction of the cost of a new mould. Size Chart: What Fits Which Market The table below is the short version of a conversation we have every week. Capacity decides the shelf price; the neck decides which pump fits; the material decides whether the product is visible. 50-100 ml, 18/410 or 20/410, PET: serum, toner and travel sets. 250 ml, 24/410, PET or HDPE: hand soap, sanitizer, lotion. 300 ml, 24/410: body lotion. 500 ml, 24/410 or 28/410: shampoo, body wash, hand soap in commercial sizes. 750 ml, 28/410, HDPE: family shampoo and pet shampoo. 100-200 ml, 24/410, HDPE: flat bottles for pocket and travel. Two rules hold across the range. A pump needs at least 0.55 mm of wall at the shoulder, and a 28/410 neck adds roughly 4 mm of diameter, which changes the cap and the carton. If you are moving a product from 250 ml to 300 ml, the neck can stay the same and only the mould changes. What Buyers Get Wrong Buying the Closure Separately From the Bottle A pump that fits on a drawing can leak on a bottle. Test the pair. Assuming 410 and 415 Are Interchangeable Both are 24 mm; only one seals. Ask for the thread code. Over-Torque at the Filling Line Above spec the liner distorts and opens a gap on one side. Pumps, Caps and Sprayers Are Tested on the Bottle Closures are injection moulded, tested against the bottle, and sold with it. A pump that fits on a drawing can leak on a bottle, because the neck tolerance and the thread depth are what actually seal. We stock 24/410 and 28/410 lotion pumps, mist sprayers, flip-top and disc-top caps, and 18/410 and 20/410 droppers for small bottles. All are fitted and leak-tested before packing. What to Send When Ordering Closures Only The neck finish of the bottle you are using, the product viscosity, and the dose you want per stroke. If the bottle comes from another supplier, send one; we will test the closure on it rather than assume the neck is standard. MOQ is 1,000 pcs per closure type, and mixed closures in one carton are possible within the same neck size. Why Closures Leak, in Order of Frequency First: the wrong neck. A 24/410 closure on a 24/415 bottle threads on but does not seal. Second: over-torque at the filling line, which distorts the liner. Third: a liner that is incompatible with the product (oil-based formulas swell EPE liners). Fourth: a dip tube cut too long, which pushes the pump up and breaks the seal. All four are lower in unit cost to fix at the sample stage than after a container ships. That is why we test the closure on the bottle, filled, rather than sending a closure sample on its own. Matching Table by Neck 18/410: droppers, small serum bottles, 10-30 ml. 20/410: fine mist sprayers and mini pumps, 30-100 ml. 24/410: lotion pumps, flip-top and disc-top caps, 250-500 ml. 28/410: heavy-duty pumps, 500-750 ml. 43/48/53 mm: cream jar lids. 63/70 mm: food jar caps with induction liners. Lead Time and Packing Closures are made to order in the same plant: 25-35 days after sample approval for standard pumps and caps, plus 5-7 days for a custom colour. They ship fitted to the bottles where possible, which removes one packing step and one damage claim at the filling line. Ordered separately, closures pack 1,000-2,000 per carton depending on size; a 24/410 lotion pump is 1,000 per carton and weighs about 12 kg. For repeat orders, we keep the closure specification on file with the bottle drawing, so a reorder two years later uses the same thread tolerance rather than a lookalike from another mould. Run the spec checker → Get Price in One Business Day → Download Catalogue Which Dropper, and Why It Matters More Than the Bottle The pipette decides the dose and the complaints. A rubber bulb is cheap and perishes; a push-button holds the dose and costs 20–30 % more. For a stable oil, a bulb dropper is fine. For retinol, vitamin C or anything sold on precision, the push-button is the better answer. Bulb Cheapest, familiar, and the part that fails first in a humid bathroom. Push-Button A button on top draws a fixed dose; no rubber to perish. About 20–30 % more per unit. Bottle Material: PET or Glass Glass is inert and reads premium; it is also heavier and breaks. PET is a third of the weight and cheaper to ship, which is why most 30 ml serums now ship in PET with a glass pipette. What to Send in a Brief Capacity, closure type, quantity and the product's viscosity. For oils, tinctures and refills, say whether the pack is sold singly or in a set — sets need matched label positions across sizes. Closure Testing Screw cap is tested on the filled pack before packing, because the closure is what fails first in the field. Decoration and MOQ Silkscreen from 1,000 pcs; spray coat and metallising from 3,000. A stock colour keeps the first order small. Compatibility, Packing and Tolerance Closures That Fit Send the neck finish and we match a closure from the same plant: disc-top and flip-top caps, lotion and foam pumps, mist sprayers and droppers. Payment is 30 % deposit, 70 % against the bill of lading. Tolerance Dimensions hold to ± 1.5 % and weight to ± 1 g against the approved drawing. Anything outside that range is remade, not discounted. Decoration Options and What They Cost in MOQ Silkscreen in one to four colours starts at 1,000 pcs and adds about five days; the plate is a one-off, which is why it does not repeat on a reorder. Labels are lower in unit cost for multi-colour artwork and allow short runs. Hot stamp, spray coat and metallising start at 3,000 pcs because the line set-up is heavier and the reject rate is higher. Decoration also decides the recycling story. A paper label with a wash-off adhesive keeps a PET bottle in the PET stream; a full-body sleeve does not. If the pack carries a recyclability claim, the decoration is part of the claim, not a design detail. Sampling and Approval A sample from an existing mould takes 7 days and comes from the production tool, not a showroom piece. For a new shape, tooling takes 15–20 days before sampling. We ship the sample with the drawing it was made to, so the approval is against a number rather than a photograph. If the formula contains alcohol, a high level of essential oil or a particulate, say so at sample stage — the compatibility test runs four weeks and it costs less to find a problem then than in a container. How We Quote and Ship Send capacity, neck, quantity and the closure you intend to use. We reply within one business day with unit price, packing data (pcs per carton, carton size, gross weight) and lead time — the packing data is what your freight forwarder needs, so it is quoted with the price rather than after. Production is 25–35 days after sample approval on existing moulds, 15–20 days longer if a new mould is needed. Payment is 30 % deposit and 70 % against the bill of lading; FOB Shantou is the default term, EXW and CIF on request. Send a dieline or a reference photo and we come back with a price within one business day. What Buyers Get Wrong Hot Fill in Standard PET Above about 60 °C the bottle deforms. Heat-set PET or PP/HDPE is the answer. Orifice Chosen After the Cap A 3 mm orifice for sauce, 8 mm for dressing, none for juice. It is a cap decision made with the filling line. Documents per Family, Not per Batch The declaration covers the resin lot. Ask per order. Cold Fill and Hot Fill Are Different Bottles Standard PET handles cold and ambient fill. Above roughly 60 °C it distorts unless the bottle is heat-set, which is a different mould and a different price. For hot sauce and pasteurised juice, the honest options are heat-set PET or PP/HDPE. Most juice and sauce in PET is cold-filled and preserved by pH, preservative or chill chain. If your process is hot fill, say so before we quote — otherwise the first pallet will deform. Necks, Orifices and Closures Sauce bottles use 38 mm or 43 mm necks for filling speed; juice uses 28/410 or 38 mm with a tamper-evident cap. The orifice insert controls flow: a 3 mm orifice for sauce, 8 mm for dressing, none for juice. For food contact we supply the resin declaration of compliance and can quote a migration test on the finished bottle where the destination market requires it. Why Food Bottles Cost More Than Cosmetic Bottles Food adds requirements rather than materials: a wider neck (more resin), a heavier wall for filling-line handling, and documentation. The bottle itself is usually 10-20 % more expensive than the cosmetic equivalent at the same volume. Frequently Asked Is your PET suitable for hot fill? Standard PET distorts above about 60 °C. For hot fill we quote heat-set PET or PP/HDPE instead. Do you provide food contact documentation? Yes — the resin declaration of compliance, and a migration test on the finished bottle where the destination market requires it. What neck is standard for juice bottles? 28/410 for 250-500 ml juice, 38 mm where filling speed matters. What is the MOQ for food bottles? 1,000 pcs per colour, 25-35 days after sample approval. Text: Jars — 250–500 ml | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Products / Jars 250–500 ml Jars, and Why the Lid Liner Decides the Seal Wide-mouth PET jars for dry food, spices and supplements. Tamper-evident options. 2 SKU Capacity All 250 500 Material All PET Neck All 63 mm 70 mm 250 ml PET Food Jar 63 mm · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → 500 ml PET Food Jar 70 mm · PET MOQ 1,000 pcs · 25–35 days View → What Buyers Get Wrong Skipping the Liner Decision Oil-based creams swell EPE liners. Specify the liner with the jar, not after the first leak. Double-Wall Thread Depth The thread sits on the outer shell; a liner that fits a single-wall rim may not sit flat. Frosting as a Colour Frosting is a surface treatment, not a colour — it does not add a changeover, and it does not hide a yellowing resin. Cosmetic Jars and Food Jars Are Different Products A cosmetic jar is sold by fill weight (30 g, 50 g, 100 g) and judged by the weight in the hand and the sound of the lid. A food jar is sold by volume and judged by whether the seal holds and how fast it fills. They share a mould shop, not a specification. Cosmetic jars are usually single-wall PET or double-wall PETG. Double wall costs more and feels expensive; it is also heavier to ship. Food jars are PET for cold fill and PP where the product goes in hot. Sealing, and Where Jars Fail For cosmetics, the thread and the liner decide whether the cream leaks into the cap. For food, an induction seal liner needs a flat land on the rim; not every jar design has one, and that is worth checking before you print the carton. Hot fill above roughly 60 C distorts standard PET. For jam and sauces we quote PP, even though clear PET looks better on shelf. MOQ and Colour 1,000 pcs per colour on existing moulds. Frosting is a surface treatment, not a colour, so it does not add a changeover; spray coat and metallising start at 3,000 pcs. Single Wall, Double Wall, and What the Rim Does A single-wall jar is one moulded piece: lighter, costs less, and is the standard for volume skincare. A double-wall jar has an outer shell and an inner cup, so the product never touches the decorated surface and the wall can feel thick without using more resin than necessary. The rim is where both types fail. Cosmetic jars need a flat land for the liner; food jars need a land wide enough for an induction seal. A 63 mm food jar with a 2 mm land seals reliably; a decorative rim with a 1 mm land does not, and no amount of torque fixes it. Sealing Methods Compared Screw cap with a PE gasket: lowest unit cost, recloseable, fine for creams and dry food. Screw cap with an induction liner: a foil membrane seals to the rim, visible tamper evidence, needs a flat land, adds about USD 0.02-0.04 per jar. Pressure-sensitive liner: easier to apply, easier to reseal unnoticed, weaker tamper evidence. For export food, induction is the safer conversation; for cosmetics, a gasket and a good thread are usually enough. Decoration and Packing Frosting is a surface treatment and starts at 1,000 pcs; spray coat, metallising and hot stamp start at 3,000. Jars stack well in cartons, which keeps freight lower than bottles of the same volume: a 250 ml jar ships about 300 per carton against 200 for a 250 ml bottle. If the jar is double wall, the outer shell and inner cup are packed assembled; the carton quantity is based on the assembled height, not the shell alone. The choice is about the formula's hardness and the user's habit, not about cost. Where Balm Containers Fail The twist mechanism either slips under pressure or clicks loose in a bag. A mechanism with a positive detent costs a few cents more and removes the complaint. Second failure: the balm sweats in heat. A PP body handles a car interior better than a thin PETG one. What Buyers Get Wrong Expecting Glass Luxury From Plastic PETG reads closer to glass than PET, but it is not a flacon. Use it for travel, testers and refills. Crimp or Screw Decided Late Crimp prevents refill and tampering; screw allows both. The neck differs, so it is decided before tooling. Dose per Spray Ignored 0.05–0.1 ml per spray changes the perceived strength of the scent. Specify it with the pump. Plastic Atomizers, Honestly Described A plastic perfume bottle is not a glass flacon. It is PET or PETG with a crimp or screw atomizer, and its advantage is weight and freight, not luxury. For travel sizes, testers and refill formats it is the practical choice; for a flagship 100 ml scent it is not. Thick-wall PETG reads closer to glass than thin PET, at roughly 20-30 % more per unit and 3,000 pcs MOQ for the heavier wall. Crimp or Screw A crimp pump is sealed to the bottle and cannot be refilled; a screw pump can. Crimp is the perfume standard because it prevents tampering and evaporation; screw is used for travel and refillable formats. The choice changes the neck: crimp bottles have a specific collar diameter, so the pump and bottle are ordered as a pair. Send a dieline or a reference photo and we come back with a price within one business day. What Buyers Get Wrong Trigger on a Mist Bottle A 28/410 trigger does not fit a 24/410 mist bottle. The neck is decided by the sprayer. Foam Without a Foaming Agent A foam trigger needs a low-viscosity formula; a thick gel will not foam whatever the nozzle. Solvent in a Standard Sprayer Degreasers and high-alcohol formulas attack the gasket. Say so at the sample stage. Trigger, Mist and Foam: Three Different Products A trigger sprayer is a pump the hand squeezes; a fine mist sprayer is a pump the finger presses; a foam trigger mixes air at the nozzle. They share a bottle and nothing else. A 28/410 trigger will not fit a 24/410 mist bottle, and a foam head needs a low-viscosity formula or it will not foam. Most home-care and garden lines use 500-1,000 ml HDPE bottles with 28/410 triggers; cosmetic mists use 100-200 ml PET with 24/410 or 20/410 fine mist sprayers. The bottle is chosen by the sprayer, not the other way round. What Decides the Cost The sprayer is usually 40-60 % of the unit cost at 1,000 pcs, not the bottle. A standard trigger is a few cents; a pre-compression continuous sprayer can be ten times that, which is why continuous spray is reserved for premium products and 3,000+ pcs runs. Bottle weight is the second lever. A 1,000 ml HDPE at 55 g and at 75 g look the same on a shelf and differ by about 20 % in resin cost. Testing Before It Ships Two failures dominate returns: the trigger leaking at the nozzle after a few hundred strokes, and the dip tube cut too long so the bottle does not stand flat. We test the fitted unit filled, 20 strokes, and check the tube length against the bottle base. If the formula contains a solvent (degreasers, alcohols), say so — it changes the gasket material inside the sprayer. Frequently Asked What is the difference between a trigger sprayer and a fine mist sprayer? A trigger is squeezed by the hand and delivers a stream or spray for cleaning products; a fine mist sprayer is pressed by a finger and delivers a cosmetic mist. They use different neck sizes and cannot be swapped. What bottle size do trigger sprayers use? Most triggers are 28/410 and suit 500-1,000 ml HDPE bottles. Cosmetic mist sprayers are usually 24/410 or 20/410 on 30-200 ml PET. Can you supply the sprayer with the bottle? Yes — trigger, mist and foam sprayers are fitted and tested on the bottle before packing. What is the MOQ for a spray bottle? 1,000 pcs per colour for stock moulds; continuous sprayers and new shapes start at 3,000 pcs. Where 4 Oz Is the Right Size Travel sets, sample sizes, hot sauce and condiment packs, and one-handed craft or workshop products. It is also the size that fits a retail peg without a carton. What Closure to Specify A 24/410 disc-top with a small orifice for gels, a 38 mm sauce cap for condiments, or a silicone valve cap when drip-free dispensing matters. How It Is Priced Weight is the first lever: a 4 oz LDPE runs 18–26 g depending on wall, and that difference is roughly 25 % of the resin cost. Colour is the second: stock white or natural costs nothing extra; a matched colour adds a changeover at 1,000 pcs. Decoration is third. Silkscreen from 1,000 pcs, labels cheaper for multi-colour artwork. Packing density is fourth, and it decides the freight more than the unit price does. Text: Squeeze Bottles — LDPE & HDPE, 30–500 ml | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Products / Squeeze Bottles LDPE · HDPE Squeeze Bottles, and Why the Valve Stops the Drip 30–500 ml soft-wall and firm-wall squeeze bottles for sauces, gels and cleansers. 4 bottle types Item Material MOQ Notes LDPE squeeze bottle LDPE 1,000 pcs Soft wall, 30-250 ml HDPE squeeze bottle HDPE 1,000 pcs Firmer wall, 100-500 ml Sauce squeeze bottle LDPE 1,000 pcs Wide 38 mm neck, 8-24 oz Dropper squeeze bottle LDPE 1,000 pcs With 18/410 dropper tip Quoted per artwork and quantity. Send a dieline or a reference photo and we come back with a price within one business day. What Buyers Get Wrong LDPE Where the Bottle Must Stand Soft-wall LDPE collapses as it empties. For shelf presence, use HDPE. Sauce Neck Too Narrow 38 mm is the filling-speed standard; a 24/410 sauce bottle slows the line and clogs the orifice. No Valve in the Cap Without a silicone valve, thick sauces drip after dispensing — the most common complaint. Soft Wall or Firm Wall LDPE is the soft squeeze: it collapses as it empties, which suits sauces, gels and anything dispensed by pressure. HDPE is firmer and springs back, which suits lotions and products where the bottle should keep its shape on a shelf. The test is simple: fill it, squeeze it, and see whether it returns. A sauce bottle that does not return looks cheap; a lotion bottle that collapses looks broken. Necks and Dispensing Sauce bottles use a wide 38 mm neck for filling and a small orifice cap for dispensing. Dropper squeeze bottles use 18/410 with a tip insert. Cosmetic squeeze tubes and bottles sit in between at 24/410. If the product is thick, a silicone valve in the cap gives a clean cut-off and stops the drip that customers complain about. MOQ and Colour 1,000 pcs per colour on stock moulds, 25-35 days. LDPE takes colour well but shows flow lines on translucent shades; opaque white and black are the safest first order. Frequently Asked LDPE or HDPE for a squeeze bottle? LDPE if the bottle should collapse as it empties (sauces, gels); HDPE if it should spring back and keep its shape (lotions). What neck does a sauce squeeze bottle use? Usually 38 mm for filling speed, with a small-orifice cap or a silicone valve for clean cut-off. Can squeeze bottles be used for cosmetics? Yes — 30-250 ml LDPE with 24/410 or 18/410 closures, common for cleansers and travel products. What is the MOQ? 1,000 pcs per colour, 25-35 days after sample approval. ## https://8pck.com/projects/four-part-mixing-pack/
Title: Four-part mixing pack — case note | 8PCK
Description: A 200 ml four-part pack: collar-carried threads, two O-rings, a left-hand joint and what the sample round caught.
Sections: Decision 1 — the Collar Carries the Threads; Decision 2 — Two O-Rings, Not One Gasket; Decision 3 — the Lower Joint Is Left-Hand; What the Sample Round Caught; Questions
Text: Four-part mixing pack — case note | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Projects / Four-part mixing pack Case · four parts · 200 ml A Four-Part Mixing Pack, and the Three Decisions That Decided It Body, upper cup, collar and base, with two sealing joints. The moulds were the easy part; the joints were the project. Item Specification Parts 4 moulded + 2 silicone O-rings Moulds 4, single cavity Body material PETG, clear, 1.8–2.0 mm Decorative parts ABS, champagne-gold vacuum metallising Sealing Two O-rings in the collar, one per joint Threads Upper right-hand, lower left-hand Tooling time 38 days Decision 1 — the Collar Carries the Threads The first sketch had threads on the body and on the cup. That forces two injection bodies with thick walls. Moving both threads onto a separate collar let the vessels stay blow-mouldable, which cut tooling and unit cost at the same time. Decision 2 — Two O-Rings, Not One Gasket A flat gasket on each joint needs a wide land and a flat face; the vessels had neither. Two O-rings in the collar, one above and one below, gave the seal without changing the body. The groove is 1.5–1.6 mm deep for a 2 mm cord, 20–25 % squeeze. Decision 3 — the Lower Joint Is Left-Hand With both joints right-handed, opening the cap loosened the body: a filled pack in a bathroom is enough to do it. The lower thread was reversed so the opening load tightens instead of releasing. It is a one-line change on a drawing and a different mould mechanism. What the Sample Round Caught The first samples sealed at the collar and wept at the cap: the plated ABS cap had a 0.2 mm step at the sealing face, invisible until the vacuum test. A tool correction fixed it, and the plating was moved off the sealing face entirely so the same failure cannot return on a reorder. Building Something With More Than One Part? Send the section and the closure — we return the stack and the seal plan. Send a Section → We use Google Analytics to see which pages buyers actually read. No ads, no cross-site tracking. Allow Analytics No thanks QUOTE ✆ WhatsApp Get a Quote → Questions Why a separate collar instead of threads on the body? It keeps the vessels blow-mouldable, which cuts both tooling and unit cost. Why is one thread left-hand? So opening the cap tightens the other joint instead of loosening it.

Item Specification Capacity 500 ml + 100 ml Material PET, clear Neck 24/410 on both Closures One lotion pump family, two dip-tube lengths Tooling 2 moulds, 24 days One Neck, Two Bottles Fixing both bottles on 24/410 meant one closure purchase, one torque setting and one spare part. Text: Thick-wall 30 ml serum bottle — case note | 8PCK Shantou · China +86 133 6387 9944 ISO 9001 · EU 10/2011 · RoHS joe@8pck.com 8PCK EN Request a Quote Menu Home / Projects / Thick-wall serum Case · one part · 30 ml A 30 ml Thick-Wall Serum Bottle That Had to Feel Heavier Than It Was Premium is a weight and a shadow. Both are decided by the wall and the base, not by the resin. Item Specification Capacity 30 ml Material PETG, clear Wall 2.2 mm at the body, 3.5 mm at the base Neck 18/410, dropper Weight 48 g Tooling 1 mould, 26 days The Base Does the Work A thick wall alone reads as plastic. The weight in the hand comes from a solid base: 3.5 mm at the bottom, tapering to 2.2 mm at the shoulder. That taper is also what stops the sink marks that a uniformly thick base would show. The Dropper Had to Reach the Last Millilitre A 30 ml bottle at 2.2 mm wall has less internal depth than a thin one. The pipette was shortened 4 mm and the tip angle changed so it reaches the base without touching it — a 15-minute mould change that avoided a "cannot get the last dose" complaint. Why Not Glass Glass would have been heavier and cheaper per unit at this volume, and the customer knew it. The decision was freight and breakage: 48 g of PETG ships at a quarter of the weight and arrives intact. Want the Premium Feel Without Glass? Send the volume and the target weight. Three things that cause most first-order failures: whether the neck fits the closure, whether the capacity suits that neck, and whether the wall is thick enough for a pump stroke. Why does wall thickness matter? A 500 ml bottle at 0.45 mm flexes under a pump stroke and the pump starts drawing air. 0.55 mm is the practical floor; 0.65 mm where the pump is large or the bottle is 750 ml.
